explanation: Fires on a wide, unrelated mix of tokens: math operators and fraction pieces in LaTeX/code (\geq, %, mod, exponents), 'range' in medical statistics, 'the' in sports phrases, 'Apache' in license headers, legal '(Id.)'. No shared trigger is apparent.

Mostly fires in code and technical text at structural boundaries: blank lines after a closing brace or #include/\documentclass, 'at' in stack traces, import/namespace keywords, identifiers like $provide or logger. It also fires on some news-prose function words ('the', 'at least', 'to'). The overall picture is mixed, but it leans toward code-structure positions.

Fires on 'food' (strongest when capitalized, as in 'Food and Drug Administration' or 'Food and Beverage'), and more weakly on 'Bio'/'bio' and on 'Technological'/'technology'/'Information' inside institution or field names. In short: the domain word in names of industries, agencies and fields (food, bio, tech).

Fires on a diffuse set of content tokens, mostly in scientific or biomedical prose: word-piece continuations ('carbon[ic]', 'cry[op]reserved', 'estr[adi]ol', 'eff[lux]') and nouns or verbs after a determiner or preposition ('paying', 'severity', 'self', 'interest'), plus code identifiers like cookieValue. No clear single trigger.

Fires strongly on 'not' in the conditional 'if not' of GPL license boilerplate ('if not, write to the Free Software Foundation'), and in general on 'if not' / 'If not,' constructions. It also fires on other conditional or restrictive clause words in license and legal text (license, purposes, code, longer). Weaker on commas after conditional clauses.

Fires on many unrelated things: 'binary' in 'source and binary forms' in BSD licenses, '-moz' CSS prefixes, operators in arithmetic word problems, 'of' in 'for the love of God', 'public' key, possessives 'my'/'his'. It is a mixture with no clear common trigger.

Fires on declaration and definition keywords in code headers (#define after #ifndef include guards, #pragma, @interface, @dataclass) and on '-exclusive' in 'non-exclusive' license grants. It also fires on technical qualifiers in math or science ('finite', 'uniformly', 'weak lens'). Broadly: formal or technical definitional context, but heterogeneous.

Fires on a heterogeneous set of tokens with no obvious shared trigger: digits inside numbers, variables in math expressions ('*p', '*z'), 'http[://]' in license headers, CSS class suffixes, ordinary prose words ('to', 'want', 'be', 'instead').

Fires on a broad mix: the comma in 'source and binary forms, with or without' and 'Permission is hereby granted,', 'com' after import in Java, and many mid-sentence function words in prose ('the', 'to', 'is', 'or', 'not'). There is a modest tendency toward commas and conjunction points in boilerplate legal text, but overall it is diffuse.

Fires on the first token of a document body right after a title line and blank line, typically the start of a Wikipedia-style article repeating the title ('Šeduva

[Š]eduva', 'Lisnadill

[L]isnadill', 'In [the] theory of'). Also fires on early tokens of a new question or line in math problems. Elsewhere it is weak and scattered.

Fires on the first word-piece of a word split into several tokens, especially Latin-derived legal or formal words ('rem'and/'rem'edy, 'Att'orneys, 'am'eliorate) and foreign names or words ('Lux'emburgo, 'carr'erai). Also fires on some function words in legal or foreign-language text ('is hereby', 'si').

Fires on an inner word-piece of rare, multi-token words or proper names, often foreign or technical (Kanan[ask]is, Cioc[col]aterie, poly[dipsia], Heisenberg, Crockett, INRIA, Russian subword pieces). Weak on ordinary words. Some license-text tokens ('OF ANY KIND') appear as offshoots.

Fires on the domain suffix in URLs, above all '.org' in 'http://www.boost.org' in Boost license headers, and also '.com'/'.co'. It also fires on other sub-token pieces inside identifiers, names and non-Latin script (isempty, Gold[stein], .Object, Greek and Japanese byte pieces). Mainly the second piece of a dotted or compound identifier.
